identity.title: Stemmer sign: inability to pinch a skin fold at the base of the 2nd toe

technique.how: With the patient supine or seated, try to lift a fold of dorsal skin at the base of the second (or third) toe between thumb and index finger; compare with the other foot (or the hand for arm swelling). Positive when the skin cannot be pinched into a fold or the fold is markedly thickened.
technique.prerequisites: Visible dorsum of the foot; compare sides; note BMI and duration of swelling because obesity and long-standing venous disease thicken the skin.
technique.contraindications: None; avoid forceful pinching over ulcerated or infected skin.

interpretation.positive_finding: Inability to pinch the toe-base skin fold supports lymphedema (recomputed sensitivity 0.89, LR+ ~2.5 in a lymphoscintigraphy-referred cohort) and argues against pure venous, cardiac or hypoalbuminaemic edema, though obesity and neuromuscular disease can mimic it.
interpretation.negative_finding: A pinchable fold lowers the probability of lymphedema (LR- ~0.17) but early stage 1 lymphedema in lean patients can be missed.
interpretation.pitfalls: False positives with obesity (BMI >40) and immobility; false negatives in stage 1 disease and normal BMI; in undifferentiated swollen limbs any single classic sign has low sensitivity (17% for the composite of signs), so a negative Stemmer does not exclude lymphedema.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive in chronic unilateral swelling: lymphoscintigraphy and search for pelvic/inguinal malignancy or prior nodal surgery; negative: pursue venous (DVT/insufficiency) and systemic causes.

estimates.target_condition: Lymphedema (primary or secondary, arm or leg) confirmed by lymphoscintigraphy
estimates.population: 110 consecutive patients (mean age 35 y, range 1-88; 90 lower limb) referred to a tertiary lymphedema program, single senior examiner
estimates.reference_standard: Lymphoscintigraphy (delayed tracer transit to inguinal/axillary nodes or dermal backflow)
estimates.computed_from: 2x2 from Results: TP 80, FP 7, FN 10, TN 13. Sensitivity = 80/90 = 0.889; specificity = 13/20 = 0.65; LR+ = 0.889/0.35 = 2.54; LR- = 0.111/0.65 = 0.171; prevalence = 90/110 = 0.818. The paper labels 80/87 (0.92) as 'sensitivity' and 13/23 (0.57) as 'specificity' - those are PPV and NPV
estimates.quote: positive Stemmer sign (n = 87) exhibited abnormal (n = 80) or normal (n = 7) lymphatic function by lymphoscintigraphy (sensitivity = 92%)

estimates.target_condition: COMPOSITE: >=1 classic clinical sign of lymphedema (dorsal hump, square toes, Kaposi-Stemmer sign, nonpitting edema) for lymphoscintigraphy-confirmed lower-limb lymphedema
estimates.population: 436 swollen limbs (of 636 consecutive) undergoing lymphoscintigraphy at a venous/lymphatic referral practice, retrospective
estimates.reference_standard: Lymphoscintigraphy (transit delay, dermal backflow, collaterals, node uptake)
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.17/(1-0.88) = 1.42; LR- = (1-0.17)/0.88 = 0.94; prevalence = 258/436 abnormal lymphoscintigraphy = 0.59; from reported sensitivity 17% and specificity 88% of the composite of signs
estimates.quote: Sensitivity and specificity of clinical signs in predicting lymphoscintigraphy-confirmed lymphedema were 17% and 88%, respectively.

sources.citation: Goss JA, Greene AK. Sensitivity and Specificity of the Stemmer Sign for Lymphedema: A Clinical Lymphoscintigraphic Study. Plast Reconstr Surg Glob Open 2019;7:e2295.
Jayaraj A, Raju S, May C, Pace N. The diagnostic unreliability of classic physical signs of lymphedema. J Vasc Surg Venous Lymphat Disord 2019;7:890-897.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Acute unilateral swelling - the Stemmer sign says nothing about DVT; obtain compression ultrasound first.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: New lymphedema in an adult without prior nodal surgery/radiation should prompt evaluation for obstructing pelvic or inguinal malignancy.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Goss 2019 used a single expert examiner; no interobserver agreement reported. Jayaraj 2019 found Kaposi-Stemmer sign the only individual sign predictive of lymphedema (odds ratio 7.9, P = .02; Abstract) but present in only 32% of limbs with any sign.

extraction_notes: Goss 2019 (PMC6635205 open access) reports 'sensitivity = 92%' and 'specificity = 57%', but the counts in the Results (positive sign n=87: 80 abnormal, 7 normal; negative sign n=23: 10 abnormal, 13 normal) show these are PPV (80/87) and NPV (13/23). The estimate entered uses the recomputed 2x2 (sens 80/90 = 0.889; spec 13/20 = 0.65) and is flagged computed=true. Prevalence 0.818 reflects a tertiary referral cohort (spectrum bias; 20 of 110 had normal lymphoscintigraphy) - high pre-test probability limits generalisation to ED edema. Jayaraj 2019 reports accuracy only for the composite of classic signs (entered as COMPOSITE), not for the Stemmer sign alone; Stemmer sign alone was present in 32% of the 96 limbs with any sign (Abstract). Search 'Stemmer sign lymphedema sensitivity specificity' returned only these two accuracy studies plus a 2025 lipedema-vs-lymphedema CART paper (PMID 40009424) not extracted.
